HRA Analysis: BETTOR BE BOHDI (1) led and ran third recently at Marburg in a race taken out by Barracuda. He has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead early. He has run a lot of placings but does seem to struggle to win. NORTHVIEW CRUNCHA (8) should get a good run through behind the likely leader in the race. He got back and couldn’t get into the race last time out which was taken out by Son Of Xena over the 2138. He should be more suited from this draw and over the 1660. FIGHT FOR VICTORY (7) loomed up and looked the winner recently before being run down by Son Of Xena. He draws poorly outside the front row in this race and will need a few things to go his way in the run. RACANA (3) has good gate speed and was able to lead recently over the 2138 before being run down late by Next To Me. She draws well but will start outside a number of gate speed horses in this race which looks awkward for her. SELECTIONS: BETTOR BE BOHDI (1), NORTHVIEW CRUNCHA (8), FIGHT FOR VICTORY (7), RACANA (3) SUGGESTED BET: BETTOR BE BOHDI (1) to win.

THE REAL ROCKETMAN (9) led last time out before handing over and running a good second behind Rocky Leigh. He is likely to get a good run off the speed in this race and can be running on well late. MAYWYNS KAREN (6) sat close to the speed last time out and wasn’t beaten far by Rocky Leigh in fourth over the 2138. The draw looks quite awkward for her in this race but she is going well and should be too far away. VICTREE BUSTA (5) finished a close up fourth last time out behind Galvarino at Marburg. He draws awkwardly in this race but finds suitable company and with the right run could figure in the finish. STONES (10) was able to run on well last time out at Redcliffe when getting back and finishing it off well into third behind Surprise Baby. He should get the right type of run again in this race. SELECTIONS: THE REAL ROCKETMAN (9), MAYWYNS KAREN (6), VICTREE BUSTA (5), STONES (10) SUGGESTED BET: THE REAL ROCKETMAN (9) to win.

SWEET ROCKY (7) led two starts ago and appeared to have his chance there when beaten by Amami. He then made a break last time out and finds himself ODM as a result in this race. He should be able to press forward in this race and can bounce back. PUNTERS JEWEL (6) got back last time out and was running on fairly late at this track when finishing fifth. He draws awkwardly this time and may get back and will need the race run to suit. MY ULTIMATE VICTOR (2) has good gate speed and should be able to zip across and lead early before having options from there. He led three starts ago and was run down late by One Last Roll there. LLANFAIR LLEWELLAN (1) doesn’t have much gate speed which could see him crossed early and shuffled back which could make things tough. He was forced to race without cover last time out when well beaten but could be better suited over the shorter trip. SELECTIONS: SWEET ROCKY (7), PUNTERS JEWEL (6), MY ULTIMATE VICTOR (2), LLANFAIR LLEWELLAN (1) SUGGESTED BET: SWEET ROCKY (7) to win.

FIRE AND PASSION (6) was forced to race without cover last time out and just couldn’t quite reel in Williams who has been racing in excellent form. He finds a suitable race where he should be able to press forward and find a prominent position and should be very hard to beat. CHARGE AHEAD (4) secured a good run last time out and was charging through before running into trouble at a crucial stage. If he had clear running he likely would’ve won last time out and if he can secure the right run in this race he should go well again. FIRE RAISER (7) has been impressive in recent outings including an excellent fourth when stepping right up in grade behind Leap To Fame before making a break at his latest outing which took him out of play. He draws poorly in this race and would need a lot to go his way. FIFTY THREE STARS (9) has been impressive this time in racing in strong company. He led two starts ago and was able to prove too good there for Quik Change over the 2138. He can be running on late this time. SELECTIONS: FIRE AND PASSION (6), CHARGE AHEAD (4), FIRE RAISER (7), FIFTY THREE STARS (9) SUGGESTED BET: FIRE AND PASSION (6) to win.

POCKET BOOK (2) has gate speed and may be able to press forward in this race and lead before having options from there. She is usually best suited when sat up and saved for one run and should be hard to hold out in this race. OCTOBER RACKETEER (4) led last time out and set a very fast tempo there before tiring late but he was entitled to. He should be able to press forward again in this race and if he could secure a more economical run in front he can bounce back this time. MACS A DUDE (10) took on a strong race last time out which was taken out by Mighty Deal at this track and trip. He should get a good run off the speed in this race and should be running on late if the race is run to suit. HARRY KANE (3) secured a good run off the speed last time out and was running on fairly late there. He should settle closer this time and can be hard to hold out late. SELECTIONS: POCKET BOOK (2), OCTOBER RACKETEER (4), HARRY KANE (3), MACS A DUDE (10) SUGGESTED BET: POCKET BOOK (2) to win.

WARRAWEE FLYER (1) found a good spot on the pegs last time out before being badly held up for clear running when appearing to have plenty left to give late. She draws favourably in this race and can look to drive through and lead early. BETTOR CHEER (11) had a tough run outside the leader last time out and wasn’t beaten far there in fifth. He finds a suitable race but does draw poorly and may need to do work at some stage of the race. SHE MAYBE BETTOR (12) got back last time out and was running on well there into fifth. She is likely to be shuffled back in this race and can be running on well late. SMIRKS LIKA BOSS (9) got back in the run last time out and was running on strongly behind Mighty Ideal. He should get a similar run in this race and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: WARRAWEE FLYER (1), BETTOR CHEER (11), SHE MAYBE BETTOR (12), SMIRKS LIKA BOSS (9) SUGGESTED BET: WARRAWEE FLYER (1) to win.

MAGIC MIKI (5) draws the best of the main chances in this race and may be able to press forward and find the lead early. He trialled up well recently when just dashing up the straight late to beat trotter Raffie Jay. He should be hard to beat. BENNYDASOOK (9) led recently at this track and trip when rolling along a very genuine tempo and being run down by King Bling finishing third. He is likely to get a good run off the speed in this race and can be running on late. AMYLEE (8) trialled up well recently finishing third behind smart stablemate Fire And Passion. She was impressive in her latest race start when finishing second behind Stripes in the QBRED Triad final. SWEET NELLIE JOY (2) should have the speed to drive through and lead before potentially taking a sit on one of the favoured runners. With the perfect run just behind the speed she looks to have good place claims in a race of this nature. SELECTIONS: MAGIC MIKI (5), BENNYDASOOK (9), AMYLEE (8), SWEET NELLIE JOY (2) SUGGESTED BET: MAGIC MIKI (5) to win. OVERVIEW: This is a very even race with plenty of chances to open the meeting. ELIZAJANE (9) is in brilliant form, having won three of her last five starts. All of her recent wins have come when she has found the front. She will have a different race map here, but it should still suit her. She has the best sectional times in this event. BREATHE EASY (1) has great gate speed and is racing well. He has the option to hold the front or take a sit, but he is suited over the short trip. INTERPRETATION (7) is racing well despite her only fair numerical form. She has faced some tough race maps recently and comes up against another tricky barrier here, but with some luck, she is a winning chance. MISTER JIMARINGLE (5) was restricted for racing room late last start but looked to be letting down nicely. He is racing well and, if he can map favourably here, he is a great chance. Also respecting YANKEE MOJOH (11), who is flying at the moment. However, barrier 11 over the short trip at Kilmore will be difficult to overcome. SELECTIONS: ELIZAJANE (9), BREATHE EASY (1), INTERPRETATION (7), MISTER JIMARINGLE (5)

OVERVIEW:KIMCHI (9) drops in class here, having not contested an NR up to 40 race in quite some time. He has been racing well, has a good relationship with driver Taylor Youl and should be able to follow through at the start. THE LADYBIRD (5) was an eye-catching winner at Horsham last start. She found a good position midfield, was saved for one run and flew home to win nicely. If she can find a similar race map here, she can go back-to-back. MIKI MARK (7) is racing consistently well and has rarely finished outside the top five recently. He faces a tricky barrier here. TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6) is an interesting runner. At his last two starts, he has worked hard to find the front and tired a little late. He has the best last sectional times in this field. If he can slot into a good position without being used too hard early, he will be a threat late. Also respecting LAVADA GOLD (2) here. SELECTIONS: KIMCHI (9), THE LADYBIRD (5), MIKI MARK (7), TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6),

OVERVIEW:THREE SIX THREE (2) is a very well-bred colt making his debut. He is by Captaintreacherous out of Art De Triomphe, making him a brother to Gawn and Petillante. He used the sprint lane to win a trial at this track in late September, although it was in slow time. We will learn more about his ability here, and whatever he does, he will likely improve from the experience. AMANDO (3) is having his second career start. On debut, he tired and dropped out before being sent back to the trials. Although the trial was run in slow time, the way he won looked impressive. I am happy to give him another chance here. ELLIANA (11) came close to breaking through for her maiden victory on several occasions last preparation. She is first-up here and will be vulnerable from the tricky barrier, but she is one of the better horses in this field on exposed form. HEAVENLY NIKKY (9) is another horse who has come close to breaking through for her maiden victory on several occasions. She is racing well and now comes up against a tricky barrier, so she will need some luck to find clear running late. However, she is a winning chance here. SELECTIONS: THREE SIX THREE (2), AMANDO (3), ELLIANA (11), HEAVENLY NIKKY (9)

OVERVIEW:CRACKIN PHILTRA (4) has had only three career starts since November 18, but they have all been good runs. He returned to the track in October, racing in the breeze and fighting on strongly. He will improve with fitness and appears to be a classy type. LIBERTY STAR DUST (7) has the best sectional times on exposed form in this field. He finished second last start behind Cyclone Jenni at Cranbourne after flashing home. With the right run, he will be flashing home again. TRYX VIXEN (3) is a smart filly who is racing well and suits barrier three. ULTIMATE GRANGE (6) is having his fourth career start here. Forget his last run, as he had a flat tyre. His previous start was a nice win at Ballarat. I also have plenty of respect for JANSEN (5), who rarely runs a poor race. TOSWEETTOTAME (2) is a first starter here, but his trial form has included some well-beaten efforts. BACK: CRACKIN PHILTRA (4)– 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: CRACKIN PHILTRA (4), LIBERTY STAR DUST (7), TRYX VIXEN (3), ULTIMATE GRANGE (6)

OVERVIEW:MELICAN (6) is an exciting young filly for Rebecca Barley. She has had two career starts for two wins, with a cumulative winning margin of 44.9 metres. We are yet to discover her ceiling. FOREGONE CONCLUSION (1) is an experienced performer stepping out for his 205th start. He is racing well and should get a good run along the fence here. ALTIUS (2) is in great form after winning nicely first-up last start. With his great gate speed, he is likely to find the fence here. CATIES SON (8) is first-up but is the only horse on the back row. He has options from there. I also respect THE BLAZINBOOTS (7), who is in great form but faces a poor barrier. BACK: MELICAN (6)– 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: MELICAN (6), FOREGONE CONCLUSION (1), ALTIUS (2), CATIES SON (8)

OVERVIEW:TOBYS SHOUT (7) was ultra-impressive last start at Wagga. He was wide early, worked forward to the breeze and was simply too good late. He has the best sectional times in this event. The barrier is a concern, but he can make his own luck. ROCK POSTER (5) is third-up here and should be approaching peak fitness. She was too far back to get into the race last start, while at her previous outing she ran home nicely for third at Ballarat. She should improve with fitness but will need some luck from the barrier. THEROUX (3) found his best form last start to win at Ballarat. He was three-back on the fence, got wide late and ran home well. He has his winning confidence back. MISS PIGGY WIGGY (6) led and won nicely last start at Shepparton. She is unlikely to find the front here, but she is racing well. Keep an eye on HIGHVIEW HAMMER (4) early. He has good gate speed and, if he can map well, he also comes into contention. SELECTIONS: ROCK POSTER (5), THEROUX (3), TOBYS SHOUT (7), MISS PIGGY WIGGY (6)

OVERVIEW:TALKNPLAY (4) was first-up last start since December 2025 and was also making his debut for new trainer Mark Thompson. He led and was too good late. Expect an improved performance here with added fitness. KNOW THE SCORE (3) can be forgiven for his last start, when he galloped due to a gear malfunction. Prior to that, he had been racing quite well. He has a nice turn of foot. REASON TO LAUGH (5) has won two of his last three starts and is in career-best form. He is a good swooper and, if saved for one run, will be flashing home. SHEZABLUECHIP (6) raced in the breeze to win well last start at Shepparton. She faces a tricky barrier here but can make her own luck. SELECTIONS: TALKNPLAY (4), KNOW THE SCORE (3), REASON TO LAUGH (5), SHEZABLUECHIP (6)

OVERVIEW: This is a nice race, with every horse in the field appearing to be a progressive type with an exciting future. DECODE (6) is a nice horse for Chris Svanosio. He finished eighth last start in a Victoria Derby heat, running home nicely despite it being his first look at the 2760-metre trip. He is a very talented horse and ran a brilliant 1:50.7 at Wagga the start prior. Back to the shorter trip here, he will be hard to beat. DELIGHTFUL MIKI (5) ran home nicely to finish a respectable third at Melton last start. She is a smart mare. Abby Sanderson has two runners in this event, CAPTAIN MOLLY (1) and THE WISE GUY (7), and both have plenty of ability and look to be progressive types. However, both are first-up and may need the run. CAPTAIN MOLLY (1) is suited by barrier one and should get a good trip. THE WISE GUY (7) has not raced since August 2025, so he may be vulnerable from the barrier. STORM VENDETTA (2) won in nice time last start at Ballarat. He has a great turn of foot, but this is a tough race. BACK: DECODE (6)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: DECODE (6), DELIGHTFUL MIKI (5), CAPTAIN MOLLY (1), STORM VENDETTA (2) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:HOOKLINEANDSINKER (2) has improved with every start since returning from a spell and worked forward to find the lead when he scored at Globe Derby last outing. He is drawn to lead again and should take catching over the sprint distance. CALF PEN (6) has returned to his peak form having been placed at his past four attempts. He worked hard when second at Mildura two starts ago then followed with a third against a strong line up at Horsham. ALWAYS ON SAFARI (5) is a fast beginner and has been racing well enough to feature prominently. He held his own after having an economical run at his latest third in South Australia. LOWER MANHATTAN (11) was placed twice in succession prior striking trouble at Globe Derby last outing. He is poorly drawn but should be finding the line well SELECTIONS: HOOKLINEANDSINKER (2), CALF PEN (6), ALWAYS ON SAFARI (5), LOWER MANHATTAN (11)

OVERVIEW:BETTORBUST (10) is a smart juvenile that should strip fitter from his first up fourth at Wagga, where he raced greenly in the early stages and eventually took cover behind the leader. He performed extremely well at the trials prior and he appears to be well suited against this line up. SNEAKY PHILTRA (9) returned to her peak form when she sprinted home best to win over ACCELERE (6) and CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (2) at Mildura last outing. She is awkwardly drawn but should be finding the line strongly again. CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (2) performs best when he is able to lead and finally gains the right draw to obtain a prominent position so he is worth an investment. MY ULTIMATE HENRY (1) delivered a career best performance to win at Mildura last outing and is drawn to receive the perfect trip so he must be respected. BACK: BETTORBUST (10) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BETTORBUST (10), SNEAKY PHILTRA (9), CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (2), MY ULTIMATE HENRY (1)

OVERVIEW: SHEER ME (3) pushed forward to find the lead and won comfortably at Kilmore then followed with an unplaced run against a strong field at Wagga. She should give a bold showing from her good draw at her Mildura debut. HILLTOP CRUNCH (5) followed a fourth in the SA Australian Gold Final in June with a win in the Sales Classic at Port Pirie. He is widely drawn but is a promising juvenile and should run a good race again. SURETHING (4) is resuming since a Mildura victory back in June and hasn’t been to the trials. She is a nicely bred filly and has the ability to figure in the finish. LIKE A LIBRARIAN (1) will appreciate her best draw for a long time and is a possible improver. SELECTIONS: SHEER ME (3), HILLTOP CRUNCH (5), SURETHING (4), LIKE A LIBRARIAN (1)

OVERVIEW: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (6) began quickly and pushed forward to find the lead when he won comfortably at his first run since June. All of his ten career victories have been at Mildura and he is the class runner of the field so he can overcome the poor draw. LETSGO BIG GIRL (2) performs best when she is able to lead over the sprint distance so she has the conditions to suit her here. She finished off solidly from the second half of the field when a close third at her latest Mildura performance. DALLAS MIKI (5) is resuming since a third at Mildura in July but he led throughout at a recent trial success. He is very strong and likes to roll along at a genuine tempo so he is sure to make his presence felt. PRIORITISE (8) endured a tough run when a creditable fourth behind Wipeout at Mildura after a second behind My Ultimate Jimmy. He is worth thought along with DEMON BLUE (7), which is making his local debut. SELECTIONS: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (6), LETSGO BIG GIRL (2), DALLAS MIKI (5), PRIORITISE (8)

OVERVIEW:THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) is racing in outstanding form and looms as the horse to beat again despite the awkward draw. He won by nearly 30m at Gawler, fought very hard when second in the Mildura Guineas then scored comfortably at Mildura last outing. LISTEN TO THE HAND (3) led throughout in two victories at Mildura and Gawler prior to an unplaced effort in the Mildura Guineas. He disappointed last time out but is capable of better and should give a forward showing. FOXY TWO GLOVES (4) is resuming since a sixth behind Dallas Miki in March. She was racing against much tougher opposition when she was last in work so she is capable of featuring prominently if she is somewhere near her peak. MIDNIGHT PIRATE (5) led out then took cover when second behind THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) last outing. He might not be able to get across to the markers from his awkward draw here but he is racing well enough to be competitive. BACK: THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: THE GOLDEN HOOK (7), LISTEN TO THE HAND (3), FOXY TWO GLOVES (4), MIDNIGHT PIRATE (5)

OVERVIEW:YARRAMAN JOLT (3) is a speedy pacer, which has performed well in two Mildura attempts, which has yielded a win and a third. He is ideally drawn for this assignment and should give a bold showing. MY ULTIMATE BILLY (7) hasn’t won a race since March 2024 but he is better than that statistic suggests and appears to be well graded in this event so he is not without a chance. ROYAL SAXON (8) scored after trailing the leader two starts ago then was caught behind tiring runners at his latest sixth. He prefers to race close to the pace so being drawn on the second line is a disadvantage but he is likely to be strongly fancied. SHES POPPY (4) is rising in class on her latest good performances but she is fast beginner and is drawn to be prominent throughout. SELECTIONS: YARRAMAN JOLT (3), MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (7), ROYAL SAXON (8), SHES POPPY (4)

OVERVIEW: THE END (7) is a nicely bred colt, which has shown a lot of ability at the trials and strikes a very suitable assignment first up. He won at his latest trial appearance over the smart filly Sabalenka at Shepparton. LATHER WITH FIRE (4) wasn’t beaten by far at her first two Mildura appearances prior to her latest two efforts in the South-East. She appears to be better suited under these conditions and is worth thought. MISS CULLEN (3) ran a better race after trailing the leader at Mildura last outing and is a good chance of finding the same position from her good draw so she must be considered as a place chance again. FEARLESS SNIPER (5) should have benefited from her first up performance at Swan Hill, where he finished eighth but didn’t perform badly and is not without a chance. SANTA CASA LEVI (6) is resuming from a spell and hasn’t been to the trials but she is a speedy type and is worth thought in multiple combinations. BACK: THE END (7) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: THE END (7), LATHER WITH FIRE (4), MISS CULLEN (3), FEARLESS SNIPER (5)

OVERVIEW: EAGLEYE (7) settled midfield and made ground out wide on the track when third behind Bettor Doo at Shepparton last outing. She was placed behind Soho Amaryllis in a much stronger race at Melton on September 18 so she appears to be hard to beat against this line up. FLEUR BELLA (3) raced without cover throughout, pulled hard and produced a big performance to win at Mildura last outing. She was impressive last time and will take plenty of catching if she is able to find the lead. SUNSHINE WARRIOR (5) led throughout to score at Mildura on September 27. He was safely held behind FLEUR BELLA (3) at his latest attempt but he is worth another chance. BIG BAD CHAD (2) is resuming since July but he was able to win a trial at Mildura recently and performs best when he is close to the speed so he cannot be discarded. SELECTIONS: EAGLEYE (7), FLEUR BELLA (3), SUNSHINE WARRIOR (5), BIG BAD CHAD (2)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG CRIPPA (6) has been promising a win for some time and will be aided by the small field of seven runners so he must be considered as one of the leading chances. He attempted to lead throughout when second behind the South Australian pacer Keilah two starts ago then got a long way back from a similar bad draw at his latest appearance. HESASTAR (7) was able to lead throughout at Mildura three starts ago and this race is of similar standard. He is likely to make a move once the pace slackens during the middle stages and is worth an investment. BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (5) is a fast beginner and will appreciate a drop back in class for this assignment. He was runner up at Swan Hill on Thursday after leading out then taking cover and should give a forward showing under these conditions. DIAMOND KRUSHER (4) led throughout at a Mildura victory four starts ago and is not without a chance from her reasonable draw. SELECTIONS: KEAYANG CRIPPA (6), HESASTAR (7), BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (5), DIAMOND KRUSHER (4)

OVERVIEW: PHILS BOY (3) was left stranded without cover and battled on well for third behind Feefifofum at Mildura last outing, beating most of tonight’s rivals in the process. He appears to be well placed against this line up and gets his chance to break through for a win. LITLMAX (1) is a first starter for trainer Brendan Tune, which scored in slow time at a recent Mildura trial effort. He is ideally drawn first up and should receive every chance. CHEDDAR CHEESE (2) was resuming since July and making his Mildura debut when fourth to Edgar Bromac last outing. He should have benefited from that performance and should give a forward showing. CRUEL MISTRESS (7) was placed from behind the leader at Mildura on August 21 and has the perfect trailing draw so she is a minor place chance again. She did run a reasonable race when fourth at Swan Hill on Thursday. BACK: PHILS BOY (3) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: PHILS BOY (3), LITLMAX (1), CHEDDAR CHEESE (2), CRUEL MISTRESS (7)

OVERVIEW: The opening event at Melton is a maiden, but there are plenty of smart horses early in their careers, making this a competitive race. MYDEEPESTDESIRE (4) has had three career starts, drawing poor barriers each time and enduring three very tough runs in narrow defeat. He clearly has ability, is tough and shouldn’t remain a maiden for long. PET WOLF (3) is another impressive, lightly raced horse. He has had four starts since December 2025 and has yet to miss a place. He has good gate speed and is likely to find the fence first here. EVA EXPRESS (2) is having her second career start. On debut, she finished fourth after flashing home nicely when popping out from a three-back-the-fence position. She should improve with the experience and added fitness. MYSTIC MOTIVER (9) covered an extra 41 metres while racing wide last start and was still rattling home late to finish second. She looks like a smart type and has been unlucky not to break through for her maiden victory. BACK: MYDEEPESTDESIRE (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: MYDEEPESTDESIRE (4), PET WOLF (3), EVA EXPRESS (2), MYSTIC MOTIVER (9)

OVERVIEW:FREAK OUT (9) is a consistent, experienced horse who rarely puts in a bad run. He can make his own luck, although he sometimes seems to lack the high speed needed late when surrounded by swoopers. He is a nice horse with a good barrier here, allowing him to follow through early and find a handy position. FAKE CULLECTION (5) is fourth-up here and should be approaching peak fitness. She got too far back last start to win, but she let down nicely and looked determined. If she can map well, she will be a threat late. BETTOR DOO (8) is a former Mildura horse who recently moved to Bendigo trainer Brent Curran. He has had two starts since the change of scenery, finishing fourth before scoring a last-start win at Shepparton, where he did it tough but was simply too good. This is his first look at Melton. He will need luck from the barrier, but he is a smart horse. BETA THAN LOVE (1) has been racing well and has the gate speed and the ideal barrier to get every chance here. SELECTIONS: FREAK OUT (9), FAKE CULLECTION (5), BETTOR DOO (8), BETA THAN LOVE (1)

OVERVIEW:CATCH THE CAPTAIN (1) is an exciting first starter. He is closely related to Catch A Wave and Yambukian and is trained by Andy Gath, who knows the family well. He won a recent Melton trial, running home in 27.5 seconds, although the first two quarters were slow. We will learn more about him here, but he has plenty in his favour. ASHANTE WARRIOR (7) was first-up for Alex Ashwood last start. He worked forward, found the lead and broke through for his maiden victory. This is a step up in class, and he has a tough barrier to overcome. YANKEE GAMBLER (5) is a tough horse who can, and often does, make his own luck. However, he is first-up since February, which could leave him vulnerable here. STAY FOOLISH (3) is a former New South Wales horse having his first start here for Paul Tonkin, who does a great job with his team. Expect improvement with the change of scenery. BACK: CATCH THE CAPTAIN (1) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: CATCH THE CAPTAIN (1), ASHANTE WARRIOR (7), YANKEE GAMBLER (5), STAY FOOLISH (3)

OVERVIEW:BELLA LOUISE (7) has been really good at her past two starts. Two starts ago, she led and won at Ballarat, while last start she was even more impressive despite finishing second. She flashed home from last and was narrowly beaten at Kilmore. Barrier seven is not ideal, but she is racing well. EL LAZZAR (3) recently gave Lochie Cook his first winner as a trainer when he let down nicely at Cranbourne two starts ago. Last start, he flashed home again but was simply too far back. If he is close enough here, his great turn of foot makes him a threat. MUSELET (5) is racing well enough and, if he can map favourably, he should be in the finish. FIVE CENT (2) was impressive last start at Maryborough, doing all the work in the breeze and fighting on well for third. Barrier is suitable, noting GIDGETT KAY (1) is EOD so FIVE CENT (2) comes out of barrier one. SELECTIONS: BELLA LOUISE (7), EL LAZZAR (3), MUSELET (5), FIVE CENT (2)

OVERVIEW: What a terrific field this is for the Scotch Notch 3YO Trotting Colts and Geldings event. NSW Trotters Derby winner PASTOR DUNBAR (6) returns and is one of the most exciting young trotters in the country. He is fast, tough and versatile. Fitness could be the query first-up. Recent Group 1 Vicbred Super Series winner HOWDY MATE (8) will have to navigate an awkward barrier, but if he gets clear running late, he will be flashing home. KYVALLEY RAY (7) is a multiple Group 1 winner who has claimed feature events in Australia and New Zealand. He was dominant in his last-start victory in the Group 1 Need For Speed Final. My only concern is his ability to trot safely throughout. Driver John Caldow suggested in his post-race interview after that win that, although Kyvalley Ray was outstanding, he did not feel the horse was safely in a trot. He is not my top selection here because he comes with that risk. THE PREACHER (5) is a very talented, high-speed horse. He was caught wide last start and did not appear to be at his best. However, if he gets a good run here, he will be flying home late. BACK: PASTOR DUNBAR (6) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: PASTOR DUNBAR (6), HOWDY MATE (8), KYVALLEY RAY (7), THE PREACHER (5)

OVERVIEW: This is a great edition of the Aldebaran Park Graeme Lang Memorial for the two-year-old trotting fillies. KYVALLEY DIXON (7) won the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final three starts ago and has been good in defeat at her past two starts. She will need to make her own luck from the barrier, but she has the class to be competitive. ZIPPIN PAST (6) is a high-speed trotter with great gate speed. She has the option to head forward early, but if she is saved for one run, she could be flashing home late. Andy Gath has two talented young trotters engaged in SNOWIN (5) and MAJARO GIRL (9). SNOWIN (5) is a very well-bred daughter of Bold Eagle who raced away to break through for her maiden victory at Ballarat last start, at just her third start. She is improving with every run. MAJARO GIRL (9) is an exciting young trotter who recently won a Vicbred Super Series heat. She has brilliant speed but can get it wrong with her manners. She has had a long campaign but is still racing well and is a major winning chance here. It is worth noting that main stable driver Kate Gath has opted to drive MAJARO GIRL (9) over stablemate SNOWIN (5). SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY DIXON (7), ZIPPIN PAST (6), SNOWIN (5), MAJARO GIRL (9)

OVERVIEW:BUNGY (3) is an interesting horse. I black-booked him as an exciting horse to follow after his first few starts. At times, he has failed to live up to that early promise, but the ability is there. Last start at Kilmore, he was held up late but absolutely flew home to finish third. TOMBEUR (2) has had one career start, producing a tough win at Cranbourne early this month. He had to do the work but was still too good. He should improve with the experience gained from that run. MY MARIONETTE (6) has nice ability when at her best. Her maiden victory last year was eye-catching, particularly the way she let down. She has continued to perform well since without winning and will need luck from the barrier. James Herbertson picks up the drive, but he knows her well, having steered her to victory in her maiden win. TRICODE (7) has the best sectional times in this field, but it will be tough for him from the barrier. SELECTIONS: BUNGY (3), TOMBEUR (2), MY MARIONETTE (6), TRICODE (7)

OVERVIEW: Another terrific field has been assembled for the Aldebaran Park Gavin Lang Memorial for the two-year-old trotting colts and geldings. REGAL GALA (5) was the last-start winner of the Mick Clover Redwood Prelude. He has brilliant gate speed, perfect manners and plenty of toughness. He looks likely to find the front here and will be hard to beat. PHOENIX REX (6) produced one of the best wins I have seen from a young trotter in my career when taking out the Group 2 QBRED 2YO Trotting Final at Albion Park on August 22. He was inconvenienced early, with driver Ryan Sanderson nearly being tipped out, but he recovered, caught the field and proved too good late. His runs since have been a little unlucky, although he has still been slightly below his best. If he brings his best, he is one of the top young trotters in the country. INSULATOR (4) is a smart young trotter who looks to have an exciting future. He recently won a Vicbred Super Series heat, defeating several horses engaged here. He is good enough to be a winning chance but may need some luck. ORLANDO VEYRON (3) was eye-catching when storming home to finish third in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final two starts ago behind Verbici and Regal Gala. Last start, he travelled to Sydney for a feature race but made a mistake with his manners. He is a very fast trotter if he gets the right run. I also would not be surprised to see an improved performance from LUXALICIOUS (2), who was good on debut last start when finishing third at Menangle behind Verbici. BACK: REGAL GALA (5) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: REGAL GALA (5), PHOENIX REX (6), INSULATOR (4), ORLANDO VEYRON (3)

OVERVIEW: This is an interesting maiden with mixed form and several first starters. GATSBY (2) has the best sectional times in this event. Last start, he let down nicely in a race won by Casterton, who looks to be a smart prospect. He has gate speed, and barrier two is ideal, although there are question marks over how quickly the horse inside him, VALLA CHEVAL (1), will begin. DIAMOND AURORA (5) is a well-bred colt from a Christian Cullen mare and by Bettors Delight, a promising pedigree cross. He has won his past two trials, including a victory at this track, and looks well placed. His stablemate SIR KITT (6) also looks well placed in this event. He has had two career starts and showed improvement to win last start behind Hoso Magic after flashing home late. Expect further improvement here. MY ROCKING HORSE (3) is an interesting filly whose ability is difficult to assess against this field. She has recently been racing in top-age-group races against superstar fillies such as Kahula, but has often been at the back of the field. Her performances outside those top-age-group races have been very good, and she should appreciate the company here. OVERVIEW:SECRET SERVICE AGENT (4) will appreciate a drop back in class for this assignment and will take beating. He had little luck from a wide draw when unplaced in the Super Series Final then raced on the outside of the leader throughout over the testing distance of 2760m in a heat of the Victoria Derby last outing. POPCORNFRIDAY (1) was held up for a run at a vital stage, angled wide at the 150m and finished strongly for seventh (2.5m) at Melton last outing. He is a short course specialist and should be reaching his peak after having two starts back from a break so he rates as a value hope. BRINGSUSJOY (3) was held up behind the tiring leader and didn’t have the best of luck when seventh at Metropolitan level last outing. She finished fast to win over Just As Well prior so she warrants respect. DONMARO (10) hasn’t produced his best form since coming from New Zealand but he should be fitter after his first up run and his form across the Tasman was good enough to be competitive here. BACK: SECRET SERVICE AGENT (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: SECRET SERVICE AGENT (4), POPCORNFRIDAY (1), BRINGSUSJOY (3), DONMARO (10)

OVERVIEW:TED BEAR (10) finished off strongly from the second half of the field when second behind Our Pinup Girl at Ballarat and followed with a seventh from a similar bad draw at Maryborough. He is likely to settle a long way back again from his similar draw here but he does strike a suitable line up. SPUN SILVER (6) continues to race in good form and should give a forward showing. She led throughout at a Kilmore victory three starts ago and attempted to lead throughout when third in a handy mile of 1.55.0 at Geelong. FLIGHT LOUTENANT (9) struck trouble at his debut for trainer Jess Tubbs after a third at Wagga. He has the perfect trailing draw and is worth another chance. HURRICANE HOOLY (3) is racing consistently and is perfectly drawn to suit her racing pattern. She was forced out very wide from the 400m and had excuses at her latest fourth. SELECTIONS: TED BEAR (10), SPUN SILVER (6), FLIGHT LOUTENANT (9), HURRICANE HOOLY (3)

OVERVIEW: BANIA (11) was heavily supported on debut but lost his chance after breaking stride at the start. He made up many lengths and did a good job to finish as close as he did so he is worth another chance. BAD GRANDMA (8) is awkwardly drawn but was impressive at a recent Melton trial victory in a mile rate of 1.58.0 so she must be respected. THE PRIVATE DEAL (5) is a former New South Wales pacer, which joins trainer Julie Douglas. She finished off quickly to win a Shepparton trial last week and she can improve on her numerical form. MILEY KAY (2) attempted to lead throughout and was run down on the line when a close second behind Cazadero at Swan Hill. This race is no harder and she is worth thought again. SEW HOPEFULL (3) led out then took cover and battled on fairly well for second behind Keayang Maricruz at Kilmore last outing. She is a maiden from 20 starts but she is a definite place chance again. SELECTIONS: BANIA (11), BAD GRANDMA (8), THE PRIVATE DEAL (5), MILEY KAY (2)

OVERVIEW: KOSIMO (8) appears to be very well placed against this line up with his claiming price of $8,000. He possesses a powerful finishing burst and his recent efforts have been in races boasting National Ratings of over 20 points higher than this event. MISTER AMERICANO (5) was resuming from a spell when fifth at Cranbourne, where he was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off fairly well. He performed nicely at the trials prior and should go well against this opposition. LE GASTON (4) led throughout and scored over Storm Vendetta (won since) at Cranbourne on September 13. He has drawn poorly in two starts since and is capable of returning to winning form here. LENARD ESS (6) was suited by a genuine tempo in the early stages and ran over the top of his rivals to win in a mile of 1.55.5 at Geelong last outing. He has won three of his past five starts and should be finishing off nicely again. BACK: KOSIMO (8) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: KOSIMO (8), MISTER AMERICANO (5), LE GASTON (4), LENARD ESS (6)

OVERVIEW:TWIGSTAR (4) is a very promising filly that remains undefeated in two attempts and is the horse to beat again. She worked forward to find the lead and completely dominated her rivals at her latest Cranbourne success in a mile rate of 1.57.0. ARZALI ROCKSTAR (3) produced a big performance to score after racing on the outside of the leader throughout at Geelong last week. She is likely to be driven in a forward manner again and must be considered as one of the leading chances. BRAVE ART (2) copped plenty of pressure in the leading role and did a good job to hold down second in the race won by Lenard Ess last outing. She should give another bold showing from her good draw. OZZIE DIAMOND (1) failed to run on as expected last outing but she won at her two attempts prior and is worth another chance from the pole position. SANDELTON (7) remains undefeated in two starts but a negative swing in the barrier draw will make it a tougher task this evening. She did defeat ARZALI ROCKSTAR (3) at her latest success so she is not to be underestimated. BACK: TWIGSTAR (4) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: TWIGSTAR (4), ARZALI ROCKSTAR (3), BRAVE ART (2), OZZIE DIAMOND (1)

OVERVIEW:TASTE IT (3) led throughout at a Shepparton victory on September 01 and finished second from behind the leader at Shepparton last week. She is drawn to obtain a prominent position again and should go well. ALPHA CRUCIS (7) is poorly drawn but will appreciate a drop back in class for this assignment. He was held up for a run at a vital stage and used the sprint lane when an unlucky fifth (2m) at Melton two starts ago. LOAN SAILOR (8) was resuming since a win at Stawell when she galloped away and lost her chance at Geelong. She is not without a chance if she delivers a fool proof display. CHALKNCHEDDAR (4) ran a reasonable race from three back on the markers at Swan Hill last week and is worth a ticket each way in an open race. SELECTIONS: TASTE IT (3), ALPHA CRUCIS (7), LOAN SAILOR (8), CHALKNCHEDDAR (4)

OVERVIEW: MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (6) appears to be extremely well graded in this event and is clearly the horse to beat. He followed an eighth behind Bulletproof Boy in the Smoken Up Sprint with a strong effort in a heat of the South Australian Cup on Saturday night. JUSTALITTLESIP (5) was making ground out wide on the track but was severely checked with 150m remaining and lost his chance at Swan Hill last outing. He is also well placed in this event and should improve on his numerical form. IMA TERMINATOR (2) is a versatile pacer, which has the ability to show up under these conditions. He ran a reasonable race when fifth behind Ultimate Vinnie (won again since) in fast time at Ballarat last outing. PAS GUARANTEE (4) was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off well for fourth when resuming. He should be fitter from that run and is capable of filling a place. BACK: MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (6) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (6), JUSTALITTLESIP (5), IMA TERMINATOR (2), PAS GUARANTEE (4)

OVERVIEW: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (5) was resuming since March when she took advantage of a soft trip and finished off best to win at Geelong. She was in good form at the end of her last campaign and commenced her current preparation nicely so she should prove hard to beat again. CHINSKI (1) was attempting to hold the inside advantage but was checked and galloped on the first turn when an unlucky fifth at Geelong. He races best when he is able to lead so he has the conditions to suit him here. MASSIF CENTRAL (2) is also a fast beginner, which should be prominent throughout. He won from behind the leader at Kilmore three starts ago. GATESYS MATE (7) performed below expectations when he was resuming from a spell but this is a drop back in class and his form last preparation was good enough to be competitive under these conditions. SELECTIONS: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (5), CHINSKI (1), MASSIF CENTRAL (2), GATESYS MATE (7)

OVERVIEW: Tricky maiden to start the program, with the exposed form a little underwhelming, mixed in with a few runners returning from a break or making their debuts. MY ROC (7) is a 2yo who’s had plenty of experience at the trials and most recently looked quite furnished, showing speed. The stablemate who just beat him there has since shown good race form. The draw is no luxury, but he was nice off the arm in the trials, so he may still take up a forward position. JASPER JAY (6) is a 2yo in his second preparation and was runner-up in a trial to a horse who’s raced well since. He had some form around decent types last time in, so if he’s forward enough, he should run well. ARTIES COURAGE (5) was well beaten on debut, but to be fair, they went quickly and the quinella horses are above-average types. She had trialled well prior, so I’m happy to give her another chance. DYGANALI (1) has the best of the exposed form and was sound to the line last time when 3rd. A soft draw and the most in-form driver at this track appeal. SELECTIONS:MY ROC (7), JASPER JAY (6), ARTIES COURAGE (5), DYGANALI (1)

OVERVIEW:LEONARD (2) is a very quick beginner and looks an easy leader here, which is a good starting point. He was a winner here five runs back using that pattern over this distance, and while the time wasn’t overly flash, he can maintain an advantage over his main dangers, who are drawn a little awkwardly. KRISSY (7) could easily appeal on the win line based on her current form, which has been good, particularly her win three back where she burned the candle at both ends. It’s just the draw that sees her having to work hard. Her 2nd here two runs back has proven a good form race, producing winners since. MAJOR ORION (8) is crying out for a win since he came back to Victoria from Queensland, and he’s been racing well from better draws where he can be up on the pace. He’ll need the breaks to come at the right time, but he can’t be underestimated. OUR BELLA LUCIA (9) is hard to assess because she wasn’t great first up, but her form last campaign when Herbertson was aboard saw her win at Melton in a time that would win this. She must be kept safe. IM DUSTEE (1) is not a quick beginner, but if he can hunt hard to hold the leader’s back, he would come into it. However, he is still up in class, so I prefer him on the minor line. BACK: LEONARD (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:LEONARD (2), KRISSY (7), MAJOR ORION (8), OUR BELLA LUCIA (9)

OVERVIEW:ANIMADO (6) could be open to sharp improvement here, back to a suitable grade from a draw where he can be driven forward and race on the speed, which he loves to do. He’s found a couple of bad set-ups and run into a couple of sharp ones this preparation. Now rock-hard fit at his favourite track and distance, he can prove hard to beat. SASSY GABBY (4) is an interesting runner first up here off an okay trial, and she only had the one run last preparation for a 3rd before having another break. She’s displayed talent and gets Herbertson to drive, so she warrants respect despite lacking fitness. HEZ HARRYWHO (3) is a fast beginner who likes this track and distance, and although he can be a little hard to catch, his racing pattern will keep him in it for a long way. OVER THE LINE (7) has been racing well but has a terrible draw to contend with here, so he goes on the minor line. FULL CRUNCH AHEAD (8) hasn’t been trialling well, and although his exposed form may attract some market support, I’d prefer to see him at this stage. BACK: ANIMADO (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:ANIMADO (6), SASSY GABBY (4), HEZ HARRYWHO (3), OVER THE LINE (7)

OVERVIEW:KRAKEY (6) is up in grade on the ratings scale, but to be fair, this isn’t an overly strong race. He really connected with Liam Older last week, showing terrific gate speed and strength, which was more akin to his form last season. A repeat of that will see him hard to beat. WHERES WOOD WOOD (4) has never raced better than she has this season, winning six of her 16 races this year. She’s been versatile in how she’s gone about her business too, so the draw suits. ALTA BAYAMO (9) can be a little hard to catch and may be better off the front row, but he is slightly down in grade and Herbertson takes the drive, so he will no doubt have admirers and is in the mix. SHEZABLUECHIP (5) has been in good form, winning two of her last three, and does best when she can race up on the pace, so she is map dependent. BACK: KRAKEY (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:KRAKEY (6), WHERES WOOD WOOD (4), ALTA BAYAMO (9), SHEZABLUECHIP (5)

OVERVIEW:DONA AMALIA (7) was a winner back in February, and that was the last time she partnered with James Herbertson. Despite the draw, this looks to be a suitable line-up with several unreliable types. If she brings her manners, she can be hard to beat. SKYVALLEY BOY (2) has a strong SP profile in four runs for the new stable but has been a little unreliable when it comes to getting the job done. His 2nd first up suggests he’s doing well enough for this level, so if you’re willing to take the risk, he’s a chance. ABBIE (8) is a little awkwardly drawn but has been consistent overall without winning. She’s normally a grinding type, so she will need luck working into the race but is in the mix. ALDEBARAN MISTIQUE (3) can begin well and potentially take up a forward position here. She was a winner at Kilmore five runs back from that position and has been sound since then, particularly when she gets near the lead. KIMBERLYS TREE (6) can show gate speed and talent, but she just hasn’t trotted well in her last couple. Her SP profile suggests she should be considered, and CLASSIC FAIR (9) was good winning on debut but has been a little plain since. Respect the trainer/driver combination enough to throw him into the Quaddie. SELECTIONS:DONA AMALIA (7), SKYVALLEY BOY (2), ALDEBARAN MISTIQUE (3), KIMBERLYS TREE (6)

OVERVIEW:ALDEBARAN DENBAY (5) has been near faultless in four runs for new trainer Brooke McPherson, winning three straight before his 2nd at Menangle last time, when he was a well-supported favourite and still ran well. This doesn’t look any more challenging than what he’s been taking on, so there’s no reason he can’t go on with it. SYDTHESLOTH (3) may be the X-factor here, having been out of his depth taking on the best of his age group. He’s had a freshen-up without a trial but now gets Herbertson, so he’s an intriguing market watch to see if he can turn his fortunes around. STRAIGHT TO THETOP (9) has had excuses her past couple, but she is starting to become a little costly. She’s always thereabouts, so don’t dismiss her. WAIKARE ADRIANA (7) is second up here and hasn’t had any luck with barrier draws this campaign. She does like this track, so despite needing a bit of luck, she deserves consideration. SHEZALOVER (6) is having her first run for the new stable and won a trial fairly leading into this. She is a little hard to line up but is worth keeping safe. BACK: ALDEBARAN DENBAY (5) – 4 units (win) SELECTIONS:ALDEBARAN DENBAY (5), SYDTHESLOTH (3), STRAIGHT TO THETOP (9), WAIKARE ADRIANA (7)

OVERVIEW:YELLA (7) drops in grade for this and was good last week from a bad draw, where he drifted back to last and made good ground late. He’s going well enough to win again and will need luck in running, but his performance three back is good enough to win this. TREACHEROUSTIMES (5) has a good strike rate at this track, and he can show gate speed from this draw and be driven assertively to look for the front. His best form comes when he’s able to race up on the pace. BERYLS BOOTS (4) has been in consistent form and finds a slightly better draw than he’s faced in his last couple. He’s in the mix again. JOEYS HANGOVER (3) didn’t have much luck here in his past couple, but his runs have been sound this time in, including a win three back. SELECTIONS:YELLA (7), TREACHEROUSTIMES (5), BERYLS BOOTS (4), JOEYS HANGOVER (3)

OVERVIEW:SUZYS DREAM (4) has something many of the others don’t, and that’s a recent victory, having scored at Kilmore in a similar grade to this. She will have to earn it the way the map works out, but if she gets there, it will be late. CHRISTMAS BABE (1) would be odds-on if you were betting on the leader, as she is a very quick beginner, but she often feels the pinch in the concluding stages. She will give a sight, though. JAKEE BOY (8) is hard to have on form, but James Herbertson is worth so much, particularly in a race like this where the form doesn’t stand out. BET BET HOTSHOT (7) has gate seven, which makes the map challenging to overcome, but he was a winner four runs back, so he is in the mix in a race that’s hard to be confident about. SELECTIONS:SUZYS DREAM (4), CHRISTMAS BABE (1), JAKEE BOY (8), BET BET HOTSHOT (7)
